haiku-low.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized before any Redis call, so no rate-limit counter is read or changed.
haiku-low.q2: 100 requests per minute in total on Standard, because the counter belongs to the customer and all its keys share one budget.
haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After value. The request is rejected before forwarding, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. A rejected request adds nothing to the counter, so it uses no budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. The request is counted before it is forwarded, so the 500 response still used budget.
haiku-low.q6: Fail open: the gateway forwards the request, sends no X-RateLimit headers, and emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric.
haiku-low.q7: Standard is 100 requests per minute. Enterprise is not set; Product must set it, and no Enterprise limit ships until then.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis, as one counter per customer ID shared by all six instances. Old counts are removed when the key's 60-second TTL expires.
haiku-low.q9: When the 60-second counter key expires, the window ends and the next request starts a new window. The window is fixed, not rolling.
haiku-low.q10: check_and_incr is a Lua script that Redis runs as one uninterrupted step, so the read-compare-increment cannot interleave across instances.
haiku-low.q11: It is the time left on the counter key's TTL, in whole seconds rounded up. Redis holds the TTL, so every instance gives the same value.
haiku-low.q12: Retry of the store: NOT STATED. The client gets no X-RateLimit headers; the request is forwarded and the backend response returned.

sonnet.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized before any Redis call, so no rate-limit counter is read or changed.
sonnet.q2: Only 100 requests per minute total (Standard plan), since all of a customer's keys share one budget. Enterprise limit is not set.
sonnet.q3: A 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header. The request is rejected before forwarding, so the backend does not see it.
sonnet.q4: No. A rejected request adds nothing to the counter and uses no budget.
sonnet.q5: Yes. The request is counted before forwarding, so it still used budget even though the backend returned 500.
sonnet.q6: Fail open: the gateway forwards the request to the backend anyway, sends no X-RateLimit headers, and emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric.
sonnet.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: not set yet (to be set by Product) and not implemented.
sonnet.q8: In Redis, a shared store used by all six gateway instances, keyed per customer. The counter key has a 60-second TTL, and Redis deletes it when it expires.
sonnet.q9: When the counter key's 60-second TTL expires, the window ends and the next request starts a new window with a fresh count. It is a fixed window, not a sliding one.
sonnet.q10: check_and_incr is a Lua script that Redis runs as one uninterrupted step, so two instances cannot both read 99 and both allow the 100th request. It reads the count, adds 1 and allows if below the limit, otherwise adds nothing and rejects.
sonnet.q11: It is the remaining TTL on the counter key, in whole seconds, rounded up. Redis holds the TTL, so every instance gives the same value.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED whether it retries the store. The document says only that it forwards the request, sends no X-RateLimit headers, and emits the metric, so the client gets no rate-limit information.
